I've farmed this same land in Quzhou my whole life. My sons left for the city years ago, so it's mostly me now. I have 5 mu of contracted land. At 73, I can't do heavy work like I used to — I hire the village machine service for tillage and harvesting. My back won't let me do otherwise.

I will do what I've always done: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. Everyone in this village does this rotation. I know these crops. I know when to water them, I know what problems to look for. I'm not going to try something new at my age. Cotton prices have been unpredictable, vegetables need too much daily work — I stay with wheat and maize.

For seeds, I'll go to the village supply cooperative, same as always. They carry the improved wheat variety that the township recommended a few years back — better than the old seeds. For maize I'll buy hybrid seeds, the kind that yields well here.

For fertilizer I'll put down compound fertilizer before planting and then urea when the wheat joints up. I probably use a bit more than the pamphlets say, but that's how I've always done it — I'd rather not short the crop.

Wheat needs water before the winter freeze, at jointing, and at heading — three times, maybe four if spring is dry. Maize mostly gets rain in summer, but I'll pump once or twice from the well to be safe.

I'll spray herbicide on the wheat in winter, then something for aphids and powdery mildew in spring. Maize gets one spray if the corn borer shows up.
